scope: Separate observer/waker representation refactor: opaque admitted strong/weak handles, allocation-independent borrowed notification and original captured sponsorship through final weak/private-holder release.
artifact_note: Runtime sources were frozen before all three campaigns. Their tracked runtime/harness diff identities match the final sources; subsequent changes are documentation/evidence only. Instance names are opaque identifiers; prepared_utc records actual run dates.

dimensions: actual requested observer Arc layout bytes including control header and alignment
policy.count_boundary: Reserve one bundle before allocating its fixed private holder.
policy.byte_boundary: Admit the allocator-requested Arc layout after holder creation, before Global payload allocation. Failed Global allocation rolls bytes back before permitting retry; successful backing consumes the shared allowance permanently.
policy.release_boundary: Payload destruction does not refund backing. Final weak/allocator and private-holder deallocation precede refund of the original bytes and bundle.
policy.exclusions: Fixed private-holder bytes are bounded by bundle count, not included in the Arc-byte dimension. Allocator bookkeeping, separate nested-capture allocations and aggregate principal/general-heap usage are excluded.
policy.decision: Twice a four-population planning envelope of 8192 each (6144 ordinary) for waiters, timers, event watches and pending-call CQ bridges. Overlap and weak-only retention have headroom; a quarter is trusted reserve. No existing resource-limit change or memory preallocation.
policy.cost: One extra allocator-owner word per observer handle and one fixed private-holder allocation per observer, plus admission/refund synchronization. Existing pre-admitted allocator families use a zero-sized default policy and preserve representation/admission behavior.

classification_inventory.scheduler_waker: Exact thread generation-owned WaitSponsor; reading classification adds no readiness/retirement decision.
classification_inventory.timed_wait_watchdog: Already admitted timer event original charge.
classification_inventory.pending_call_cq_bridge: PendingCall class captured at original record construction, read alongside its source under IPC.
classification_inventory.per_lp_quantum: Mandatory fixed bootstrap owner per LP; infallible boot-only construction cannot be application-triggered.
classification_inventory.generic_callback: CallOnNotify::try_new receives an explicit captured class; mandatory for_test exists only for fixtures.
classification_inventory.rule: No later numeric-ASID lookup, promotion, retirement, name or role reclassifies existing backing; no new reserve grant.

handle_layout_measurement.method: Compile actual observer owned/backing, charged allocator and resource-policy modules with a std Mutex adapter on the 64-bit host; core::mem::size_of for typed/erased ObserverRef and ObserverWeak and usize.
handle_layout_measurement.note: This measures handle representation, not holder allocator overhead. Native containing thread metadata layouts are recorded independently per architecture.

controls: Four production-handle host tests cover consuming erasure, pointer identity, borrowed notification, upgrade, original-class weak-only lifetime, concurrent final weak destruction, empty weak handles and a zero-sized align-4096 payload.

Eighteen shared allocator tests include actual over-aligned Arc header/padding admission, layout denial before payload heap access, injected Global failure rollback/retry and clone-shared single allocation allowance. Successful deallocation never revives that allowance.

Native real weak-only Probe allocations fill ordinary 49152 and total 65536 bundle ceilings. There are 128 direct heap-held bundle denials, trusted reserve, exact returned ordinary-slot reuse and complete final-weak recovery.

Native real 1024-byte inline payload allocations reach ordinary 12 MiB and total 16 MiB byte limits with count headroom. Actual Arc layouts are Probe=16 and Large=1040 bytes. Two heap-held layout controls independently reject ordinary/total byte admission before Global payload allocation while preserving the separately admitted holder bundle.

Erasure, clone, upgrade and pointer equality run with actual heap/pool guards held; borrowed notification runs after guards. Last strong destruction leaves the full original backing charge until final weak release.

At total bundle exhaustion 64 real scheduler prepare_wait attempts fail before source registration, preserving exact generation, state and zero waiter usage. Existing early/stale wake, identity/publication, scheduled wait, original deadline, timer/worker/exit, IPC CQ binding and cancellation controls use the same new handles.
qualification_limits: Pressure is serialized kernel-fixture work, not sustained hostile concurrent EL0 fairness. Native general heap OOM is not forced; shared allocator Global failure is injected on the host.

Fixed-holder bytes are count-bounded, not charged as Arc bytes. Nested captures, other non-observer weak/control allocations, payload/registry storage and aggregate principal/general-heap accounting remain open.

Borrowed notification does not authorize arbitrary callbacks beneath producer guards. Existing destructor/IRQ, latency and physical-completion G1/G4 boundaries remain; this is not blanket cleanup qualification.
SEC-07 remains partial; R7-3 aggregate principal admission, R7-4 fairness and R7-5 concurrent hostile qualification remain open.
